subject: general
question: Ravikant cycles at a speed of 12.5 km/h and walks at a speed of 3 km/h. To cover a distance of 40 km by cycle and walk both, Ravikant took 7 hours. How many of these hours were spent cycling?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__
Apply **Alligation** on speeds to find the **Time Ratio**.

Average speed = 40 km ÷ 7 hours = 40/7 km/h.

Alligation: (Cycling: 12.5) − (Avg: 40/7) vs (Avg: 40/7) − (Walking: 3).

Ratio of Time = (40/7 − 3) : (12.5 − 40/7) ⇒ (19/7) : (47.5/7) ⇒ 19 : 47.5 ⇒ 2 : 5.

Total time parts = 2 + 5 = 7 units. Since total time is 7 hours, 1 unit = 1 hour.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8fd06edab00f489f9c082c6de3cca2838b8d488cdc1fcc5f26421444d289c731.png] 
**Given:** Cycling speed = **12.5 km/h**, Walking speed = **3 km/h**, Total distance = **40 km**, Total time = **7 hours**.

**Formula Used:** Distance = Speed × Time

Let the time spent **cycling** be **t** hours.

Then, time spent **walking** = **(7 − t)** hours.

⇒ Distance by Cycle + Distance by Walk = Total Distance

⇒ (12.5 × t) + [3 × (7 − t)] = 40

⇒ 12.5t + 21 − 3t = 40

⇒ 9.5t = 40 − 21

⇒ 9.5t = 19

⇒ t = 19 ÷ 9.5

⇒ t = 2 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Alligation on Speed

When alligation is applied to speeds, the resulting ratio is always the ratio of the **Time** taken for each part of the journey.

Average Speed

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time. In this case, 40 ÷ 7 ≈ 5.71 km/h.

Relative Speed

Used when two objects move. In same direction, subtract speeds (S₁ − S₂); in opposite directions, add speeds (S₁ + S₂).</p
